title: AI for Evidence Dossiers and Literature Reviews
answer: Evidence dossiers and systematic reviews depend on finding and screening the literature. In one study a GPT-4 based system reached literature search recall of 71 to 83 percent against 14 to 23 percent for human searchers and screened 1.5 to 2.6 times faster, though results still need expert checking.

reading.body:
A GPT-4 based system found 71 to 83 percent of relevant literature against 14 to 23 percent for human searchers, and screened 1.5 to 2.6 times faster.

The gap is in recall, not speed. Human searchers in this study missed most of what the model surfaced, which reframes the task: the model is not a faster typist for a review team, it is a different first pass over the corpus. Screening throughput of 1.5 to 2.6 times matters less than the fact that the candidate set itself changes.

The data covers one study of one system, and it says nothing about precision, false positives, or how much expert checking the results required. It also does not say which literature, which review type, or how the human baseline was recruited. The finding that results still need expert checking is the operative constraint, and it is the part that keeps this inside a documented method rather than a replacement for one.

Nothing here speaks to compute, buildings, or power. The binding constraint this data describes is reviewer attention, not infrastructure.

explainer:
Evidence dossiers present the clinical and economic case for a medicine to payers and health technology assessment bodies, and they depend on systematic literature reviews that find and appraise all relevant studies. Systematic reviews are slow: searching databases, screening thousands of records, extracting data and assessing quality.

AI can raise search recall, speed screening and draft data extraction, with published studies showing substantial gains in specific settings. Assessment bodies expect transparent, reproducible methods, so the AI steps must be described as part of the review method, results verified by reviewers, and any limitations reported.
